params.place: on the map: the whole of Africa, a crack glowing down its east side

moments.what: the crack in the east glows
Africa's coast traces round in light
the crack zigzags south down the map
the two sides tint apart in two colours

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: What if Africa split in two?

params.place: on the map: the Horn of Africa, closing on Ethiopia

moments.what: the camera dives to the Horn of Africa
Ethiopia's border traces and its flag fills it
cracks open in the sand
the two sides slide apart with arrows
a ruler sign shows the rate
the arrows push again

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It already is: Africa's two plates pull apart by 8 to 9 millimetres a year.

params.place: on the map: the East African Rift from Ethiopia down through Kenya to Tanzania

moments.what: a pin marks the top of the line
AFAR writes on and the crack pulses
the camera pulls back as the rift line draws south
the line glows
EAST AFRICAN RIFT writes along it
LAKE TURKANA writes on beside the line
Kenya traces with its flag
Tanzania traces with its flag

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: It starts in Ethiopia's Afar desert and runs south as one long line, the East African Rift, past Lake Turkana, through Kenya and into Tanzania.

params.place: on the map: a clock dial standing on the rift in Kenya

moments.what: a snail crawls along the rift line
the snail's feelers twitch
a clock dial pops up on the map
its hands start to spin
the hands blur and the map shivers

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: That's slow, far too slow to feel. So what happens if it never stops?

params.place: on the map: the mouth of the Red Sea and the Afar lowland behind it

moments.what: the camera settles on the strait
waves gather at the mouth of the Red Sea
the coastline is rubbed out where the sea breaks in
the mouth of the Red Sea flashes
water pours inland across the Afar
AFAR's label sinks under the water
a depth gauge sign drops below its zero line
bubbles rise from the new sea

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: First, the sea breaks in through the Red Sea's southern end and floods the Afar, which already lies lower than the sea in places.

params.place: on the map: the rift through Ethiopia and Kenya filling with sea

moments.what: the camera turns to follow the water
a question mark pops over the water
the sea runs into the crack
the water races south down the line
it cuts through Ethiopia
it cuts through Kenya
a pen draws the new coastline on both banks
the pen lifts and the coast settles

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: Then where does the water go? It follows the crack south, through Ethiopia and Kenya, and a brand-new coastline is drawn on both sides.

params.place: on the map: the Horn of Africa breaking away into the Indian Ocean

moments.what: the camera pulls back over the Horn
the land east of the crack lights up
Somalia traces with its flag
the camera eases along the crack
eastern Ethiopia lights up with its flag
eastern Kenya lights up with its flag
Tanzania's coast lights up
the whole piece slides away east into the ocean
ISLAND writes on it
the island keeps sliding east
waves ripple round it in the open ocean

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: On this simplified map, everything to the east, Somalia, eastern Ethiopia and Kenya, and Tanzania's coast, breaks off as one giant island, drifting out into the Indian Ocean.

params.place: on the map: western Ethiopia on the shore of the new sea

moments.what: the camera swings to the west bank
Ethiopia's western half traces with its flag
a NO SEA sign stands on the land
the NO SEA sign is crossed out
a palm tree pops on the new shore
a little harbour with a boat appears on the coast
the boat sails out of the harbour
a flag goes up on the harbour
the new sea shimmers
a gull circles over the new sea

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: And here is the twist: Ethiopia, a country with no sea today, wakes up with a coast and a harbour of its own, on a sea that does not exist yet.

params.place: on the map: the Afar crack of the Dabbahu rift, close

moments.what: an hourglass stands on the map
its sand starts to run
the hourglass spins faster
the map fades back to today
a pin drops on the Afar
the camera dives to the pin
the pin on the Afar pulses
a date sign stands by the crack
the crack rips open along a ruler
a calendar flips its days
the crack gapes wider

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: How long would it take? Tens of millions of years. But one crack opened fast: in 2005, 60 kilometres of the Afar tore open in a matter of days, some cracks more than a metre wide.

params.place: on the map: the whole of Africa again, the crack glowing down its east side

moments.what: the island side pulses
the coast side pulses
a pointer swings between them
the pointer bobs
the camera pulls back to the whole of Africa
Africa's coast traces in light
the crack glows
the frame settles on the hook's map

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.say: New island or new coast: which side would you pick? Tell us below. Because one day, Africa may split in two.

disclaimer: Maps simplified. Borders as recognised by the country each video is about.
